wiki_text: As of May 2026, the US$5 billion Train 7 project had reached 92 per cent completion and was advancing into systems completion and pre-commissioning; 2026 reporting indicates commissioning is scheduled for 2027. When operational, Train 7 (with the associated Trains 1–6 debottlenecking) is expected to raise NLNG's capacity from 22 to 30 mtpa.

In June 2026, Ogun State Governor Dapo Abiodun announced that NNPC Ltd had informed the state government of its decision to revive the long-dormant Olokola LNG (OKLNG) project, alongside plans for the Olokola deep sea port and related industrial infrastructure. No development schedule, partners, or capacity configuration for the revived project had been announced as of early July 2026.

In October 2025, UTM Offshore reaffirmed its commitment to the 2.8 mtpa FLNG project at the Yoho field, stating the gas supply agreement was about 95 per cent negotiated, to be followed by the sales and purchase agreement with Vitol and then financial close and a final investment decision. The 2025 FID target lapsed without an FID; startup remains targeted for 2029.
